datasetName: Sea Watch Foundation Marine Megafauna Sightings: 1971 to present
fieldNotes: I was watching the sea from a window in a holiday house. The small waves were back lit by the last light in the clouds after sunset. Every small wave appeared black in silhouette. I was at first not sure what I saw. but then the group of three surfaced on about 6 occasions as they traversed north in front of me. Total length of time was about 90 seconds. The largest fin surfaced first. ahead of the other two. that seems like an adult with a juvenile alongside (and slightly behind)- my wife at first thought the second animal had two dorsal fins. We studied fin ID photos and the shape was a perfect match for long finned pilot whale. The body of the animals was only a bit out of the water. but you could see there was about twice as much surfacing in front of the fins compared to behind the fin. It was hard to tell size and distance. but maybe as close as 300 metres from shore.

fieldNotes: First spotted the fins close in to Lower Stoke. Reported to skipper who reported to Riverside Country Park and Harbour Master. They were in shallow water. Skipper managed to get boat land side and we gently headed them back into deep water and East along the estuary. They stopped to feed many times. By Garrison Point. approximately 3 hours and 4 miles after our first sighting. we were joined by 2 boats from the port authority from Sheerness who took over heading them out further. The last we heard on the radio. they were out by the wreck of the Montgomery. Lots of photos and video taken!

datasetName: Sea Watch Foundation Marine Megafauna Sightings: 1971 to present
fieldNotes: Vertical observation from near top of cliff.  Two calm large black cetaceans. with fin ahead of mid body.  Swimming at surface level. constant speed from south of viewing position to  north west of viewing position.  Within 30 metres of the cliff base [avoiding wind / current I suspect].  I am pretty sure pilot whales. from vertical view. fin location. bulk and colour are main discriminators. Fins more triangular [orca like] than normally shown on photographs.  But orca?  No signs of any pale area. even body breadth from head to the narrowing near the tail.  Unfortunately no photographs.

datasetName: Sea Watch Foundation Marine Megafauna Sightings: 1971 to present
fieldNotes: Transiting on yacht to Soverign Harbour from Newhaven.  Approx 1 mile south East (in deep water) off Beachy Head heading to Royal Soverign light. a pod of cetaceans in groups of two- three were seen. there were at least 8 possibly 10. It was approximately 1 hour before local high water  and the tidal stream was heading North East. We did not approach them and they did not come too close. They appeared to be feeding and did not broach or play like dolphins or porpoises. (we have previously reported cetacean sightings in this area)  from the shape of the dorsal fin. we believe they were pilot Whales.
